options.title: Monitor bed availability
options.description: Track bed availability for CTAS 2 patients over the next two weeks to understand the root cause of the monitored bed shortage and determine if a slow physician pace is the main factor.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If a shortage of monitored beds is due to high bed occupancy, pressure may shift to patients waiting in exam rooms. However, if the root cause is a slow physician pace, pressure may shift back to physicians.
options.how_we_would_know: By tracking bed availability and physician pace, we can identify the main factor contributing to the shortage and take appropriate action.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If bed availability improves and physician pace remains consistent, we can assume the initial cause was a surge in CTAS 2 patients. If bed availability remains low, we may need to explore other factors, such as staff shortages or equipment issues.

options.title: Adjust rooming pace
options.description: Explore ways to match rooming pace to clinician capacity, especially during periods of high bed occupancy. This could involve adjusting rooming priorities or considering alternative rooming strategies.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If rooming pace is adjusted to match clinician capacity, pressure may shift to patients waiting in the waiting room. However, this strategy aims to reduce the overall wait time for patients.
options.how_we_would_know: By monitoring the impact of adjusted rooming pace on wait times and bed availability, we can determine the effectiveness of this strategy.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If adjusted rooming pace improves wait times and bed availability, we can continue with this approach. If not, we may need to explore other options, such as increasing staff resources or implementing a different rooming strategy.

options.title: Implement wait-time thresholds
options.description: Trigger escalation huddles when room-to-physician wait times exceed a certain threshold. This proactive approach can help identify and address potential issues before they impact patient care.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: By implementing wait-time thresholds, pressure may shift to the escalation team, who will need to coordinate and resolve any issues. However, this strategy aims to prevent long waits and ensure timely patient care.
options.how_we_would_know: Through regular huddles and monitoring of wait times, we can assess the effectiveness of this strategy and make any necessary adjustments.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If wait-time thresholds are consistently met and there are no significant issues identified, we can continue with this approach. If wait times exceed thresholds, we may need to explore other strategies or allocate additional resources.

recommendation.rationale: Monitoring bed availability will provide valuable insights into the root cause of the monitored bed shortage. If a slow physician pace is confirmed as the main factor, we can then explore strategies to address this issue, such as adjusting rooming pace or implementing wait-time thresholds.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the monitored bed shortage is found to be primarily due to high bed occupancy, we may need to prioritize protecting reserve monitored beds for acute arrivals. Additionally, if staff shortages or equipment issues are identified as contributing factors, we may need to allocate additional resources or address these issues directly.

suggested_reviewers.why: Triage RNs are directly involved in reporting bed availability and managing patient flow.
Physicians play a crucial role in patient care and are impacted by wait times and bed availability.
The escalation team is responsible for coordinating and resolving issues that impact patient care, including wait times and bed availability.
